open-question.question: When the completion procedure's discretionary read of past work fails — its `tasks <path> --with-body` call or its `show <milestone path>` follow-up exits non-zero, as `show` does on the `-` a task line prints for a commit joining no single milestone — what does the runner do: stop the task on a fixed line with the tool's `Error:` line beneath it, as the review pass and the starting-state procedure stop on a failed read of theirs, or carry on with the task without the read, as `ask-in-milestone-context` carries on after telling the failure in prose?

When the completion procedure's read of past work surfaces an earlier milestone's decision or verified bar that carrying out the task as briefed would undo, and the current milestone's `requirements.md` does not address it, what governs the work: the brief as written, the earlier decision wherever the brief can still be met, or does the runner stop without completing the task?

When the completion procedure's step-2 read of past work fixes a criterion of the acceptance bar, does that criterion name what it was formed against (the task commit's hash or the earlier milestone's path), so the read shows in the `Task-completion:` commit body, or is it worded like any other criterion with no reference to the read?

The completion procedure's read of past work is triggered by a file the task edits rather than creates whose shape the milestone's `requirements.md` does not explain. Does the same trigger cover a file the task deletes, renames, or moves?
open-question.alternative: The trigger stays a change to the content of a file that already exists. `complete-procedure.md` says outright that deleting, renaming, or moving a file takes no read of past work, so the read is never taken for any of the three. A rename or move that also changes the file's content still triggers on that content edit, as any edit does. The trigger is the narrowest one and mechanically plain, so a runner never has to judge whether a removal counts. The sibling question on which runs the field measurement counts gets a clean population: runs that changed the content of a file that already existed. It also keeps the procedure's added text as small as the goal's one-sentence trigger. The most destructive change a task can make goes unchecked. Deleting or relocating a file that an earlier milestone deliberately placed (this repository has one: the host fixture's `milestones.fixture/` container is named so the discovery pattern skips it, and a `CLAUDE.md` invariant explains why) skips exactly the read meant to show why a file is the way it is. The brief and `requirements.md` are then the only guard.

The procedure treats deleting, renaming, or moving a file that already exists as editing it. The read is taken under the same condition as an edit: `requirements.md` does not explain the file's existence or place. It is taken at step 2 for files the task names up front and at step 3 for the rest. The query is `tasks` on the path the file has before the task. The milestones tool's log reads set `log.follow=false`, so the new path carries no history from before the move, while the old path, still in the tree when the read is taken, lists every task commit that changed it. Every change that undoes something already standing gets the same check before it is made. That includes removals, where an earlier decision that put the file there is most easily lost without anyone noticing. The tool needs no change: the old path exists in the tree when the read is taken, and `tasks` exits 0 on it whatever it lists. The trigger gets wider and the procedure's prose longer. It needs a clause naming which path to read, because reading the new path silently returns only the move commit. More completion runs then take a read whose output can be large: the sibling question on bounding large reads covers this. The measurement population sibling must decide whether these runs count.

The procedure treats deleting a file that already exists as editing it, under the same condition that `requirements.md` does not explain the file's existence. The read is `tasks` on that path, taken before the deletion. A pure rename or move, with the content unchanged, takes no read. The procedure says so, because the file's shape survives under its new path. The read targets the one case where the file's shape is lost outright and an earlier decision behind it cannot be seen in the tree afterwards. Renames and moves get no read, and no clause is needed about which path to read, since a deleted file has only the one path. Location can be a decision too: a name or place chosen so that a pattern matches or skips it, or a path other files cite. Such a decision is broken by a rename or move without a read. The line drawn between deletion and relocation is also one more distinction the runner has to apply and the measurement has to tell apart.

The procedure keeps the trigger worded as the goal states it, "a file the task edits rather than creates", and says nothing about deletions, renames, or moves. Whether one of these counts as an edit is left to the runner's reading on each run. The discretionary read is taken or not as that reading falls. No wording is added and no position is fixed before the field measurement has shown how runners actually treat these cases. The read is discretionary anyway, so the measurement can show whether a stated rule is needed. Runners will read "edits" differently, so the same deletion triggers the read in one run and not in another. For renames, a runner that does take the read may query the new path and get nothing, because the tool follows no rename. The measurement's counted population, owned by a sibling question, also becomes ambiguous for exactly these runs.

open-question.question: The completion procedure's read of past work is triggered by a file whose shape the milestone's `requirements.md` does not explain. Does a shape the project's context file explains (in this repository, a `CLAUDE.md` invariant) count as explained, so that no read is taken, or does only `requirements.md` count?

With the milestones tool unchanged, does the completion procedure bound its `tasks <path> --with-body` read on a file that many task commits changed, or is the read taken whole whatever it prints? Measured on 2026-11-10 it prints 200 lines (59,079 bytes) for `docs/skill-reference.md` and 104 lines (31,521 bytes) for `CLAUDE.md`, and it grows with every later task that changes the file.

Does the completion procedure's `tasks <path> --with-body` read carry the clause the review pass and the starting-state procedure put on their milestones-tool calls — the command written out in full, never through a variable, alias, or function of the runner's own — or does it show the full command with no such clause, as the other nine runtime files calling the milestones tool do?

In the field measurement that decides whether the completion procedure's read of past work stays discretionary, which completion runs is the read counted against: every completion run, only runs that edited a file that already existed, or only runs a reader judges to have met the trigger (an edited file whose shape `requirements.md` does not explain), which no transcript shows mechanically?

In the field measurement that decides whether the completion procedure's read of past work stays discretionary, which outcomes are told apart for each counted run — for instance the named `tasks` command run as shown, a history read the agent composed itself (`git log`, `git blame`, or `git show` on the file), and no history read at all?

Over which runs is the field measurement of the completion procedure's read of past work taken: which projects and hosts, starting from which plugin release, and how many completion runs at the least before its result is read?

What measured result makes the completion procedure's read of past work a required step instead of a discretionary one: any counted run in which the read was not taken or was composed by hand, a stated share of the counted runs, or another rule?

Where are the scripts and the report of the field measurement of the completion procedure's read of past work kept, so that its figures can be checked again later: under the git-ignored `temp/`, where the reports and scripts of the two earlier field measurements stood and no longer do, in a tracked location, or does the plan in `ideas/milestones_addressed_by_path.md` leave it unstated?
